context.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore is a globally distributed, Amazon-style e-commerce platform designed to support physical and electronic book sales, personalized recommendations, and reviews. It ensures high availability, strict security compliance, and multi-currency transactions for up to 1 million monthly active users.

## Key Elements
- Shopper (Customer): End-user browsing catalogues, managing carts, purchasing books, and leaving reviews.
- Administrator (Store Operations): Staff managing catalogue inventory, pricing, and content moderation.
- Third-Party Payment Gateway: External PCI-DSS compliant system for secure checkout and tokenized payments.
- Third-Party Shipping Provider: External logistics service handling fulfillment dispatch and tracking.
- Third-Party Currency Exchange Service: External provider supplying real-time conversion rates for USD, EUR, and GBP.
- Third-Party Recommendation Engine: External service powering "Customers also bought" cross-selling features.
- Online Bookstore System (AWS): Core software system deployed across `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, and `ap-southeast-1`.

## Relationships
- Shopper / Administrator to Online Bookstore System via HTTPS (TLS 1.2/1.3) for browsing, authentication, and management.
- Online Bookstore System to Third-Party Payment Gateway via HTTPS/REST for tokenized payment processing.
- Online Bookstore System to Third-Party Shipping Provider via HTTPS/REST/Webhooks for fulfillment and tracking.
- Online Bookstore System to Third-Party Currency Exchange Service via HTTPS/REST for FX rates.
- Online Bookstore System to Third-Party Recommendation Engine via HTTPS/REST for product recommendations.

## Technology Stack
- Cloud Infrastructure: AWS (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1) providing global reach and scalability.
- Compute & Orchestration: Amazon ECS or EKS running stateless application containers with regional HPA.
- Database: AWS Aurora Global Databases with localized read replicas to ensure low-latency reads and GDPR compliance.
- Security & Compliance: AWS CloudFront/ALB for edge termination, AWS KMS (AES-256) for data at rest, and AWS Secrets Manager for credential management.
- Observability: AWS X-Ray and OpenTelemetry for distributed tracing across multi-region services.

## Rationale
This multi-region active architecture guarantees the 99.95% uptime SLA and sub-2-second page load times required for global performance. Furthermore, isolated regional databases and strict boundary controls ensure seamless compliance with GDPR, CCPA, and PCI-DSS mandates.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
An Amazon-style online bookstore delivering physical and electronic books with recommendations, reviews, and secure global checkout. Built on AWS across multi-region infrastructure to support 1 million MAU with high availability.

## Key Elements
- Shopper and Administrator (Users)
- Frontend App (React SPA served via Amazon CloudFront/S3)
- Amazon API Gateway (Single entry point and rate limiter)
- Backend Microservices (Node.js Catalog Service, Java/Spring Boot Order & Checkout Service, Python/FastAPI Recommendation Service on AWS ECS Fargate)
- Data Persistence (Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL & Amazon OpenSearch)
- External Systems (Third-Party Payment Gateway, Shipping Provider, Currency Exchange Service, Recommendation Engine)

## Relationships
- Shopper to Frontend App: HTTPS/JSON via browser
- Frontend App to Amazon API Gateway: HTTPS/JSON with edge currency routing
- Amazon API Gateway to Backend Services: HTTPS with JWT validation via AWS App Mesh
- Internal Microservices to Microservices: gRPC over mTLS
- Backend Services to Data Persistence: TLS with IAM authentication
- Recommendation Service to Third-Party Recommendation Engine: HTTPS API calls with Envoy circuit breakers

## Technology Stack
- Cloud Provider: AWS (`us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, `ap-southeast-1`) for multi-region scale
- Compute: AWS ECS Fargate for elastic container management
- Database: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (multi-region) for transactional integrity and Amazon OpenSearch for keyword search
- Security: AWS Cognito for OAuth 2.0/JWTs, AWS App Mesh for mTLS, AWS Secrets Manager for secrets, AWS KMS for encryption at rest
- DevOps/Observability: ArgoCD for GitOps, AWS CodeDeploy for blue/green deployments, ADOT with Prometheus and Grafana for telemetry

## Rationale
Microservices on ECS Fargate combined with multi-region Aurora PostgreSQL ensure horizontal scalability for 1M MAU and 99.95% uptime. Strict subnet isolation and mTLS enforce GDPR/CCPA compliance and OWASP Top-10 mitigations while maintaining sub-2-second page loads globally.

Frontend App.analysis:
## Overview
[An Amazon-style online bookstore offering physical and electronic books with recommendations, reviews, and multi-currency support. Deployed across global AWS regions with high availability and strict security compliance.]

## Key Elements
- Shopper (User)
- Administrator (User)
- Frontend App (React SPA, Amazon S3, Amazon CloudFront, AWS Lambda@Edge)
- Amazon API Gateway (Amazon API Gateway)
- Catalog Service, Order & Checkout Service, Recommendation Service (Node.js, Java Spring Boot, Python FastAPI on AWS ECS Fargate)
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL & Amazon OpenSearch
- Third-Party Payment Gateway, Shipping Provider, Currency Exchange Service, Recommendation Engine

## Relationships
- Shopper -> Frontend App: Browses and interacts with store [HTTPS/JSON via browser]
- Administrator -> Frontend App: Administers platform [HTTPS/JSON via browser]
- Frontend App -> Amazon API Gateway: Sends API requests and localization headers [HTTPS/JSON]
- Amazon API Gateway -> ECS Fargate Services: Routes microservice requests [gRPC/HTTPS]
- ECS Fargate Services -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL & OpenSearch: Persists and indexes data [TCP]

## Technology Stack
- Frontend: React SPA, Tailwind/CSS-in-JS, `react-router`, `react-i18next`, `axios` for performance and localization.
- Hosting & CDN: Amazon S3 and Amazon CloudFront with AWS Lambda@Edge for SEO and static asset caching.
- Backend Compute: AWS ECS Fargate running Node.js, Java Spring Boot, and Python FastAPI containers.
- Databases: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL and Amazon OpenSearch for scalable data storage and search.
- Security & DevOps: AWS CodePipeline, AWS CloudWatch RUM, TLS 1.3, strict CSP, HTTP-only SameSite cookies, and OWASP Top-10 mitigations.

## Rationale
[This cloud-native architecture leverages AWS global regions, CloudFront edge caching, and serverless containers to guarantee sub-2-second page loads on 3G, 99.95% uptime, and 1M MAU scalability. Decoupled microservices ensure robust security boundaries and compliance with GDPR, CCPA, and OWASP standards.]

Amazon API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore is a scaled-down e-commerce platform providing catalog browsing, shopping carts, secure checkout, reviews, and recommendations for 1M MAU. It ensures global availability across three AWS regions while meeting strict GDPR, CCPA, and OWASP Top-10 security constraints.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Shopper, Administrator
- **External Systems**: Third-Party Payment Gateway, Third-Party Shipping Provider, Third-Party Currency Exchange Service, Third-Party Recommendation Engine
- **Frontend App**: React SPA hosted via Amazon CloudFront and Amazon S3
- **Amazon API Gateway**: Single entry point, rate limiter, and edge router
- **Backend Services**: Catalog Service, Order & Checkout Service, Recommendation Service (Node.js, Java Spring Boot, Python FastAPI on AWS ECS Fargate)
- **Data & Search**: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon OpenSearch
- **Security & Infrastructure**: AWS WAF, AWS App Mesh, AWS Secrets Manager, Amazon Route 53

## Relationships
- Shopper / Administrator -> Amazon CloudFront: Browses site and submits requests [HTTPS/JSON with TLS 1.3]
- Amazon CloudFront -> Amazon S3: Fetches static frontend assets [HTTPS]
- Frontend App -> Amazon API Gateway: Sends API requests with currency headers [HTTPS/JSON]
- Amazon API Gateway -> Catalog Service / Order & Checkout Service / Recommendation Service: Forwards requests with JWT validation and context headers [gRPC/HTTPS via AWS App Mesh]
- Services -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL / Amazon OpenSearch: Reads and writes domain data [TCP]

## Technology Stack
- **API Management**: Amazon API Gateway with native JWT Authorizers for low-latency authentication
- **Security**: AWS WAF for OWASP Top-10 mitigation, AWS Secrets Manager for secret rotation
- **Compute & Mesh**: AWS ECS Fargate containers managed via AWS App Mesh for secure service-to-service communication
- **Infrastructure as Code**: Terraform and AWS CDK for repeatable deployments across regions
- **Global Routing**: Amazon Route 53 with latency-based routing across `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, and `ap-southeast-1`

## Rationale
This architecture leverages serverless edge routing and containerized microservices to scale efficiently for 1M MAU while guaranteeing sub-2-second page loads. Multi-region redundancy and native AWS security services ensure high availability (99.95%) and strict compliance with GDPR and CCPA.

Catalog Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Catalog Service manages book discovery, search, pricing, and inventory status for the Online Bookstore. It processes high-volume catalog requests while maintaining strict security, multi-currency support, and sub-second performance.

## Key Elements
- Catalog API Controller (Express.js)
- Search & Query Engine (TypeScript)
- Pricing & Inventory Adapter (TypeScript)
- Catalog Cache Manager (Redis/ElastiCache)
- Amazon OpenSearch
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL

## Relationships
- Catalog API Controller -> Search & Query Engine: In-memory TypeScript function calls
- Search & Query Engine -> Amazon OpenSearch: HTTPS with TLS and IAM authentication
- Search & Query Engine -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: TCP with TLS and IAM authentication
- Catalog API Controller -> Catalog Cache Manager: RESP over TLS to Amazon ElastiCache
- Pricing & Inventory Adapter -> Order & Checkout Service: gRPC over mTLS

## Technology Stack
- Node.js & Express.js: Powers the Catalog Service for asynchronous request handling
- TypeScript: Ensures type safety across component modules
- Amazon OpenSearch: Delivers scalable keyword search and indexing
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Stores relational book metadata securely
- Amazon ElastiCache (Redis): Caches frequent queries and pricing to meet performance goals

## Rationale
Decomposing the Catalog Service into specialized components ensures high scalability for 1M MAU and sub-2-second page loads. Integrating ElastiCache caching and multi-region replication meets uptime and performance SLAs.

Order & Checkout Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Online Bookstore system is a scaled-down e-commerce platform for purchasing physical and electronic books with recommendations and reviews. The architecture relies on secure microservices hosted on AWS to handle global traffic, multi-currency transactions, and regulatory compliance.

## Key Elements
- Shopper and Administrator (Users)
- Frontend App (React SPA, Amazon CloudFront, Amazon S3)
- Amazon API Gateway
- Catalog Service, Recommendation Service (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Order & Checkout Service (Java, Spring Boot, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Checkout Controller / Facade, Order Management Engine, Payment & Currency Gateway Client, Fulfillment Coordinator, Order Repository, Transactional Outbox Processor (Components)
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon OpenSearch
- Third-Party Payment Gateway, Third-Party Shipping Provider, Third-Party Currency Exchange Service

## Relationships
- Amazon API Gateway -> Order & Checkout Service: Forwards order/checkout requests [HTTPS via AWS App Mesh]
- Order Management Engine -> Order Repository: Manages persistence [JDBC over TLS/IAM]
- Payment & Currency Gateway Client -> Third-Party Payment Gateway: Processes payments [HTTPS/REST]
- Fulfillment Coordinator -> Third-Party Shipping Provider: Coordinates fulfillment [HTTPS/REST]
- Transactional Outbox Processor -> AWS EventBridge: Publishes domain events [HTTPS/AWS SDK]
- Catalog Service / Recommendation Service -> Order & Checkout Service: Internal microservice communication [gRPC over mTLS]

## Technology Stack
- Java with Spring Boot: Powers the Order & Checkout Service for robust enterprise processing.
- AWS ECS Fargate & CloudFront/S3: Delivers scalable serverless container hosting and global static content delivery.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Stores transactional data securely with TLS and IAM authentication.
- Resilience4j: Implements circuit breakers to protect against third-party dependency outages.
- AWS KMS & EventBridge: Secures sensitive metadata with encryption and drives event-based cart recovery.

## Rationale
This microservices-based AWS architecture ensures 99.95% uptime across three global regions by leveraging auto-scaling containers and circuit breakers. Strict tokenization, KMS encryption, and an outbox pattern fulfill stringent GDPR, CCPA, and PCI-DSS compliance requirements while maintaining high performance.

Recommendation Service.analysis:
## Overview
[System: Online Bookstore System (Recommendation Service container). Core Purpose: Provides personalized 'Customers also bought' book recommendations for shoppers.]

## Key Elements
* Shopper
* Recommendation Service (Container, Python, FastAPI, AWS ECS Fargate)
* API Router / Component (FastAPI)
* Recommendation Orchestrator Component
* External Engine Client Component
* Recommendation Analytics & Feedback Component
* Third-Party Recommendation Engine (External System)
* Amazon SQS / AWS EventBridge
* AWS Secrets Manager, AWS X-Ray, AWS Security Groups

## Relationships
* Shopper -> Recommendation Service: Views recommendations [HTTPS via API Gateway & AWS App Mesh]
* API Router Component -> Recommendation Orchestrator Component: Forwards validated requests [Internal Python function call]
* Recommendation Orchestrator Component -> External Engine Client Component: Queries external engine [Internal Python function call]
* External Engine Client Component -> Third-Party Recommendation Engine: Fetches recommendations with circuit breakers [HTTPS API calls with Envoy]
* Recommendation Orchestrator Component -> Recommendation Analytics & Feedback Component: Emits interaction events [JSON over Amazon SQS / AWS EventBridge]

## Technology Stack
* Python & FastAPI: Core runtime and framework for fast request processing
* AWS ECS Fargate: Serverless container deployment for autoscaling
* Amazon SQS / AWS EventBridge: Asynchronous message bus for non-blocking analytics
* AWS Secrets Manager: Dynamic credential injection for external APIs
* AWS X-Ray & Envoy: Distributed tracing and sidecar proxy for telemetry and routing
* AWS Security Groups & Network Firewall: Strict egress filtering to whitelist external endpoints

## Rationale
[This architecture enforces strict separation of concerns by removing non-core currency logic and utilizing asynchronous messaging, ensuring sub-2-second performance and 99.95% availability under high load. It maintains GDPR/CCPA compliance through rigorous PII pseudonymization, least-privilege IAM roles, and secure egress filtering.]

Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL.analysis:
## Overview
An AWS-hosted online bookstore application designed to support 1 million monthly active users globally. It provides multi-currency catalog browsing, secure checkout, reviews, and personalized recommendations with strict uptime and compliance standards.

## Key Elements
- Shopper and Administrator (Users)
- Frontend App (React SPA, Amazon CloudFront, Amazon S3)
- Amazon API Gateway
- Catalog Service, Order & Checkout Service, Recommendation Service (Node.js/Java/Python, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (Multi-region database container)
- Amazon OpenSearch
- Third-Party Payment Gateway, Shipping Provider, Currency Exchange, Recommendation Engine
- Amazon RDS Proxy, AWS Secrets Manager, AWS KMS

## Relationships
- Shopper -> Frontend App: HTTPS
- Frontend App -> Amazon API Gateway: HTTPS
- Amazon API Gateway -> Catalog Service / Order & Checkout Service / Recommendation Service: REST/gRPC
- Catalog Service -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (Read Replicas): PostgreSQL wire protocol via TLS 1.3
- Order & Checkout Service -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (Primary Writer): PostgreSQL wire protocol via TLS 1.3
- Services -> Amazon RDS Proxy: PostgreSQL wire protocol via TLS 1.3
- RDS Proxy -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Internal database protocol

## Technology Stack
- Cloud Infrastructure: AWS (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1) managed via Terraform/AWS CDK
- Compute: AWS ECS Fargate for containerized microservices
- Database: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Global Database with Amazon RDS Proxy for connection pooling
- Search & Recommendations: Amazon OpenSearch
- Security & Compliance: AWS KMS, AWS Secrets Manager, IAM database authentication, TLS 1.3

## Rationale
Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with RDS Proxy provides high availability, ACID compliance, and connection scalability required for 1 million MAU. Multi-region replication and strict encryption controls ensure global low-latency performance while maintaining GDPR and CCPA compliance.

Amazon OpenSearch.analysis:
## Overview
- An Amazon OpenSearch component provides scalable keyword search, fuzzy matching, and search analytics for the Online Bookstore.
- It delivers high-performance product discovery to support 1 million monthly active users while ensuring GDPR and CCPA compliance.

## Key Elements
- **REST API Handler Component**: Receives secure HTTPS requests via SigV4.
- **Search Engine Component**: Apache Lucene Core executing inverted-index searches and multi-language tokenization.
- **Index Management Component**: Manages shard allocation, replica sync, and snapshots.
- **Data Storage Component**: EBS gp3 block storage with AWS KMS encryption.
- **Async Event Emitter Component**: Offloads search telemetry.

## Relationships
- Catalog Service -> REST API Handler: Queries catalogue items [HTTPS/JSON, TLS 1.3, SigV4]
- Search Engine -> Data Storage: Reads and writes data [POSIX block I/O]
- Search Engine -> Async Event Emitter: Offloads metrics [In-memory queue]
- Async Event Emitter -> Amazon Kinesis Data Streams: Exports search telemetry [HTTPS/JSON]

## Technology Stack
- **Amazon OpenSearch Service**: Managed search engine ensuring 99.95% availability.
- **AWS KMS**: Customer-managed keys for Encryption-at-Rest.
- **Amazon S3**: Automated snapshot storage and retention.
- **Amazon Kinesis Data Streams**: Streaming telemetry export for merchandising analytics.

## Rationale
- Multi-AZ deployment and dedicated master nodes guarantee 99.95% uptime and split-brain prevention.
- Strict IAM least-privilege scoping and private VPC isolation satisfy OWASP Top-10 and GDPR/CCPA compliance requirements.
